profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between a university population genetics lecturer and a conservation program data coordinator to prepare a GenAlEx-based Excel workbook for a half-day training session on platypus population structure and to reuse the same outputs in a river-restoration partner briefing. The context is that a new spring microsatellite run has just come back from the lab, and they want a polished workbook, example graphs, and a short analysis workflow ready within one week. The agenda is to decide which data file will be used, how the GenAlEx workbook will be prepared, what level of checking is needed before workshop materials are built, who owns each preparation step, and what the internal deadline means. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan: Alex will prepare and import the data into the GenAlEx workbook, Maya will refresh the teaching slides and example outputs, and both will work toward having a 'validated master workbook' ready by Thursday/Friday for training and briefing use.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.role: Population Genetics Lecturer and Research Lead
members.expertise: Teaching population genetics, microsatellite analysis, GenAlEx classroom workflows, interpreting AMOVA/PCoA/F-statistics
members.background: Maya runs an upper-level conservation genetics course and also supervises a small freshwater mammal genetics project; she has used GenAlEx for years as a teaching tool and often builds carefully structured Excel templates that students copy for their own analyses.
members.private_state: She wants the workshop materials done quickly without reopening sensitive data-governance questions, and she is mainly concerned that the GenAlEx file behaves smoothly for students and produces familiar population-structure patterns for class discussion.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'master workbook,' they mean her protected GenAlEx template file that individuals duplicate locally rather than a single live file everyone edits.
The 'spring platypus dataset' refers to the de-identified teaching subset from the spring field season, with recaptures removed and sites collapsed to the twelve populations used in class.

A workbook being 'validated' or having passed a 'sanity check' means the formulas run correctly, the imports do not break GenAlEx sheets, and the resulting broad patterns look consistent with prior years.
Importing genotype data into GenAlEx normally means manually placing allele-pair columns into the existing desktop Excel workbook with GenAlEx formulas already in place.
Anything used in the training session should already be safe for teaching use, so approval and de-identification are effectively settled.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: Field-data consolidation, lab result handling, Excel-based reporting, cross-team data delivery for conservation partners
members.background: Alex supports a regional river-restoration program and regularly turns field and lab outputs into briefing-ready spreadsheets for ecologists, managers, and partner agencies; he is comfortable with Excel workflows and shared-file coordination but is not a GenAlEx power user.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid version confusion, keep the partner briefing aligned with official monitoring numbers, and minimize rework by using the same source file for both the workshop and the external briefing.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'master workbook,' they mean the single authoritative Excel file on OneDrive that everyone updates and reviews as the source of truth.
The 'spring platypus dataset' means the complete 2024 spring monitoring export, including recaptures, all sampled reaches, and the location metadata used in partner reporting.
A workbook is only 'validated' once population counts, sample totals, and summary tables reconcile with the program's official monitoring tables and prior briefing materials.
An 'import' step should follow the program's usual process: clean the lab CSV into a standardized table first, then load it into the shared workbook so others can review the same live file.
Because the workbook is also for the partner briefing, it is understood that the reporting fields and management-relevant tabs stay in scope unless someone explicitly removes them.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to preparing and sharing the 'master workbook.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the protected GenAlEx template workbook that serves as the canonical layout, which others should copy and edit separately on their own machines.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the one shared, live Excel file in OneDrive that everyone will update directly and treat as the single source of truth.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many teams, 'master workbook' naturally implies an authoritative file, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the same working norm without realizing one means a template and the other means a collaborative live document.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'spring platypus dataset' they will use
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use the 'spring platypus dataset' for the GenAlEx workbook.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the de-identified teaching subset from the spring season: 96 individuals, recaptures removed, and twelve collapsed teaching populations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the full spring monitoring export: all sampled reaches, recaptures still present, and metadata retained for management reporting.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both datasets are routinely referred to informally by the same season label, and because they originate from the same field campaign, neither participant feels a need to restate the exact row count, filtering, or metadata status.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'validated' or 'sanity-checked' workbook
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the workbook should be 'validated' or at least 'sanity-checked' before Maya refreshes slides and screenshots.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a lightweight check that GenAlEx formulas, tabs, and graphs work properly and that high-level structure roughly matches expected population patterns.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a reconciliation-grade check where counts, site totals, and summary outputs match official monitoring tables closely enough to support the partner briefing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The terms 'validated' and 'sanity-checked' sound prudently aligned and are common shorthand in planning meetings, but they hide very different thresholds of completeness that only become visible during execution.

misalignment_points.topic: How the genotype 'import' will be done
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Alex will 'import the new genotypes into GenAlEx on Monday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Alex will open the desktop GenAlEx workbook in full Excel, paste allele pairs into the preformatted locus columns, and let the existing formulas and chart links propagate within that local file.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he will first normalize the lab CSV into the program's standard table, then load it into the shared workbook on OneDrive so stakeholders can review the updates in the same file.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Import is treated as routine operational work rather than a design decision, so each person defaults to their habitual workflow and hears the other's wording as compatible with their own process.

turns.inner_thought: I need the teaching file ready without getting pulled into governance or reporting scope. By master workbook, I mean my protected GenAlEx template that students copy locally; I do not want people editing one live file and breaking the formulas. The spring platypus dataset for this should be the de-identified teaching subset from spring, with recaptures already removed and the sites collapsed to the twelve class populations. And validated only needs to mean the GenAlEx sheets run cleanly and the outputs look like the familiar population-structure patterns from prior years so I can refresh slides quickly.

For me the master workbook is the shared OneDrive file that serves as the source of truth for both the workshop and briefing. Import on Monday means I'll clean the lab CSV into the standard table and load it into that shared workbook so nobody is working off different numbers.
